problem.summary: 基于点云的3D目标检测是自动驾驶、家用机器人、增强/虚拟现实等应用中的核心问题。现有方法大多依赖手工设计的特征表示（如鸟瞰图投影），这限制了模型从数据中学习有效3D形状信息和不变性的能力。

motivation.summary: 手工特征工程成为信息瓶颈，阻碍了方法有效利用3D形状信息。需要一种能够直接从原始点云中学习判别性特征表示并进行端到端3D目标检测的通用网络。

core_idea.summary: 提出VoxelNet，一个统一的端到端可训练深度网络，将特征提取和边界框预测集成到一个阶段。核心是体素特征编码（VFE）层，它将每个体素内的点组转换为统一的特征表示，从而将点云编码为描述性体积表示，再连接到区域提议网络（RPN）生成检测结果。

method.summary: 1. 体素划分：将3D空间划分为等间距体素。2. 分组与随机采样：将点按体素分组，并对每个非空体素随机采样固定数量T个点。3. 体素特征编码（VFE）层：对每个体素内的点，计算局部均值，增强相对偏移特征，通过全连接网络（FCN）转换为点特征，再通过元素级最大池化获得局部聚合特征，最后将点特征与局部聚合特征拼接。堆叠多个VFE层以学习复杂特征。4. 稀疏张量表示：仅处理非空体素，形成稀疏4D张量。5. 卷积中间层：使用3D卷积聚合体素特征，增加上下文。6. 区域提议网络（RPN）：接收卷积中间层的特征图，生成概率分数图和回归图。7. 损失函数：结合分类损失（二元交叉熵）和回归损失（SmoothL1）。8. 高效实现：通过哈希表和密集张量结构优化GPU处理。

experiments.summary: 在KITTI 3D目标检测基准上评估，涵盖汽车、行人、自行车三类。在鸟瞰图检测和全3D检测任务上，VoxelNet均显著优于现有基于LiDAR的方法（如VeloFCN、MV）以及多模态方法（MV+RGB）。在更具挑战性的3D行人/自行车检测上也取得了令人鼓舞的结果。

claims.claim: VoxelNet是首个端到端可训练的基于LiDAR的3D目标检测网络，无需手工特征工程。
VFE层能有效学习体素内的点交互和局部3D形状信息。
VoxelNet在KITTI基准上，在鸟瞰图和全3D检测任务上均大幅超越现有方法。
该网络能学习对各种几何形状物体的有效判别性表示，在行人/自行车检测上也表现良好。
提出的高效实现方法利用了点云稀疏性和体素网格的并行处理。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论局限性。潜在局限可能包括：对体素大小和采样点数T等超参数敏感；计算和内存开销仍较大；仅使用LiDAR数据，未融合图像信息；在极端稀疏或遮挡场景下的性能未详细分析。

nodes.title: 点云输入
nodes.label: 输入
nodes.summary: 原始LiDAR点云，每个点包含XYZ坐标和反射率。
nodes.description: 输入为原始点云，每个点pi = [xi, yi, zi, ri]^T ∈ R^4。

nodes.title: 体素划分
nodes.label: 预处理
nodes.summary: 将3D空间划分为等间距的体素网格。
nodes.description: 给定点云，沿Z、Y、X轴将空间划分为大小为vD, vH, vW的体素，形成尺寸为D'×H'×W'的网格。

nodes.title: 分组与随机采样
nodes.label: 预处理
nodes.summary: 将点按体素分组，并对每个非空体素随机采样固定数量T个点。
nodes.description: 将点分配到其所在的体素。由于点云稀疏且密度不均，对每个非空体素随机采样最多T个点，以平衡计算负担和密度偏差。

nodes.title: 体素特征编码（VFE）层
nodes.label: 特征学习
nodes.summary: 将每个体素内的点组转换为统一的特征表示，编码局部3D形状信息。
nodes.description: 对体素V内的点集，计算局部均值(vx, vy, vz)，增强相对偏移特征得到V_in。每个点特征通过FCN（线性层+BN+ReLU）转换为点特征f_i。通过元素级最大池化获得局部聚合特征~f。最后将f_i与~f拼接得到输出特征f_out_i。堆叠多个VFE层（如VFE-1(7,32), VFE-2(32,128)）以学习复杂特征。

nodes.title: 稀疏张量表示
nodes.label: 表示
nodes.summary: 将非空体素的特征组织为稀疏4D张量，以减少内存和计算开销。
nodes.description: 仅处理非空体素，得到体素特征列表，每个特征与空间坐标关联。表示为尺寸为C×D'×H'×W'的稀疏4D张量。

nodes.title: 卷积中间层
nodes.label: 特征聚合
nodes.summary: 使用3D卷积聚合体素特征，逐步扩大感受野以增加上下文。
nodes.description: 应用3D卷积、BN和ReLU层序列。例如，使用Conv3D(128,64,3,(2,1,1),(1,1,1))等层，将稀疏张量转换为密集特征图，用于后续RPN。

nodes.title: 区域提议网络（RPN）
nodes.label: 检测头
nodes.summary: 接收卷积中间层的特征图，生成概率分数图和回归图以预测3D边界框。
nodes.description: RPN包含三个全卷积块，逐步下采样特征图，然后通过上采样和拼接生成两个输出：概率分数图（分类）和回归图（边界框参数）。架构细节见图4。

nodes.title: 损失函数
nodes.label: 训练目标
nodes.summary: 结合分类损失（二元交叉熵）和回归损失（SmoothL1），用于训练网络。
nodes.description: 损失函数L = α * (1/N_pos) * Σ L_cls(p_pos_i, 1) + β * (1/N_neg) * Σ L_cls(p_neg_j, 0) + (1/N_pos) * Σ L_reg(u_i, u*_i)。其中L_cls为二元交叉熵，L_reg为SmoothL1。回归目标u*包括中心偏移(Δx, Δy, Δz)、尺寸偏移(Δl, Δw, Δh)和旋转偏移Δθ。

nodes.title: 高效实现
nodes.label: 工程优化
nodes.summary: 通过哈希表和密集张量结构优化GPU处理，将点云转换为适合并行计算的结构。
nodes.description: 初始化K×T×7的输入特征缓冲区。使用哈希表（体素坐标为键）高效查找和插入点。构建缓冲区后，堆叠VFE操作可在GPU上并行处理。最后将稀疏体素特征重组为密集体素网格。

nodes.title: 数据增强
nodes.label: 训练技巧
nodes.summary: 应用三种数据增强形式以减少过拟合，包括对单个边界框的扰动、全局旋转和翻转。
nodes.description: 1. 对每个地面真值3D边界框及其内部点进行随机旋转（Δθ∈[-π/10, π/10]）和平移（Δx, Δy, Δz ~ N(0,1)）。2. 对整个点云进行随机旋转（Δθ∈[-π/4, π/4]）。3. 可能包括翻转（论文未明确提及第三种，但提到三种形式）。

edges.label: 划分空间
edges.description: 原始点云被划分为体素网格。

edges.label: 分组与采样
edges.description: 点被分配到体素，并进行随机采样。

edges.label: 特征编码
edges.description: 每个体素内的采样点集通过VFE层编码为特征。

edges.label: 形成稀疏张量
edges.description: 所有非空体素的特征被组织为稀疏4D张量。

edges.label: 卷积聚合
edges.description: 稀疏张量通过卷积中间层聚合上下文信息。

edges.label: 生成检测
edges.description: 卷积后的特征图输入RPN，生成检测结果。

edges.label: 计算损失
edges.description: RPN的输出与地面真值比较，计算损失函数。

edges.label: 数据增强
edges.description: 原始点云在训练时可能经过数据增强。

edges.label: 增强后输入
edges.description: 增强后的点云进入体素划分流程。

edges.label: 并行处理
edges.description: 高效实现使得VFE层可以在GPU上并行处理。

deltas.before: 使用手工设计的鸟瞰图特征作为输入。
deltas.after: 使用VFE层从原始点云中学习体素特征表示。
deltas.why_it_matters: 手工特征是信息瓶颈，限制了模型学习有效3D形状信息和不变性的能力。VFE层允许网络直接从数据中学习判别性特征，从而在3D检测任务上获得显著性能提升。

deltas.before: 可能需要多个独立的特征提取和检测阶段。
deltas.after: 统一的端到端可训练网络，将特征提取和边界框预测集成到一个阶段。
deltas.why_it_matters: 端到端训练可以优化整个流程，避免子优化，并可能学习到更好的特征表示。

deltas.before: 处理点云时可能面临高计算和内存需求。
deltas.after: 通过稀疏张量表示和高效实现（哈希表、密集缓冲区）优化计算。
deltas.why_it_matters: 使得在GPU上高效处理大规模稀疏点云成为可能，是实际应用的关键。

formulas.name: 体素网格尺寸
formulas.latex: D' = D / v_D, \quad H' = H / v_H, \quad W' = W / v_W

variables.name: D, H, W
variables.description: 点云在Z, Y, X轴上的范围

variables.name: v_D, v_H, v_W
variables.description: 体素在Z, Y, X轴上的尺寸

variables.name: D', H', W'
variables.description: 体素网格的尺寸

formulas.intuition: 定义了如何将连续的3D空间离散化为体素网格。

formulas.name: 点特征增强
formulas.latex: \hat{p}_i = [x_i, y_i, z_i, r_i, x_i - v_x, y_i - v_y, z_i - v_z]^T \in \mathbb{R}^7

variables.name: p_i
variables.description: 原始点特征 [x_i, y_i, z_i, r_i]^T

variables.name: v_x, v_y, v_z
variables.description: 体素内点的局部均值（质心）

variables.name: \hat{p}_i
variables.description: 增强后的点特征，包含相对偏移

formulas.intuition: 通过添加相对于体素质心的偏移，为网络提供局部坐标信息，有助于学习局部形状。

formulas.name: VFE层输出

variables.name: f_i
variables.description: 点i的点特征（来自FCN）

variables.name: \tilde{f}
variables.description: 体素的局部聚合特征（通过最大池化获得）

variables.name: f^{out}_i
variables.description: VFE层的输出特征，结合了点特征和局部聚合特征

formulas.intuition: 通过拼接点特征和局部聚合特征，使每个点的表示既包含自身信息，也包含其所在局部区域的信息，从而编码点交互和局部形状。

formulas.name: 回归目标（中心偏移）
formulas.latex: \Delta x = \frac{x^g_c - x^a_c}{d_a}, \quad \Delta y = \frac{y^g_c - y^a_c}{d_a}, \quad \Delta z = \frac{z^g_c - z^a_c}{h_a}

variables.name: x^g_c, y^g_c, z^g_c
variables.description: 地面真值框的中心坐标

variables.name: x^a_c, y^a_c, z^a_c
variables.description: 锚框的中心坐标

variables.name: d_a
variables.description: 锚框底面的对角线长度，d_a = \sqrt{(l_a)^2 + (w_a)^2}

variables.name: h_a
variables.description: 锚框的高度

formulas.intuition: 对中心偏移进行归一化，使其与锚框的尺寸无关，有助于稳定训练。

formulas.name: 回归目标（尺寸与旋转偏移）
formulas.latex: \Delta l = \log(l^g / l^a), \quad \Delta w = \log(w^g / w^a), \quad \Delta h = \log(h^g / h^a), \quad \Delta \theta = \theta^g - \theta^a

variables.name: l^g, w^g, h^g, \theta^g
variables.description: 地面真值框的长度、宽度、高度、偏航角

variables.name: l^a, w^a, h^a, \theta^a
variables.description: 锚框的长度、宽度、高度、偏航角

formulas.intuition: 对尺寸使用对数变换，对旋转使用直接差值，是常见的边界框参数化方法。

formulas.name: 总损失函数

variables.name: N_{pos}, N_{neg}
variables.description: 正、负锚框的数量

variables.name: p^{pos}_i, p^{neg}_j
variables.description: 正、负锚框的softmax分类输出

variables.name: u_i, u^*_i
variables.description: 正锚框的回归输出和地面真值回归目标

variables.name: L_{cls}
variables.description: 二元交叉熵损失

variables.name: L_{reg}
variables.description: SmoothL1损失

variables.name: \alpha, \beta
variables.description: 平衡分类损失重要性的正常数

formulas.intuition: 联合优化分类和回归任务，α和β用于平衡正负样本的贡献。

main_result.description: 在KITTI验证集上，VoxelNet在鸟瞰图检测和全3D检测任务上均显著优于现有方法。

ablation.description: 通过与手工特征基线（HC-baseline）的比较，验证了端到端特征学习的重要性。
ablation.findings: VoxelNet（使用VFE层学习特征）在所有类别和难度上均大幅优于HC-baseline（使用手工鸟瞰图特征），尤其是在更具挑战性的3D检测任务上（例如，汽车3D检测Moderate难度：65.46% vs 59.75%）。

robustness.description: 论文未明确进行鲁棒性实验（如对噪声、遮挡的分析）。

scaling.description: 论文未明确讨论模型缩放（如不同体素大小、网络深度）的影响。

case_study.description: 提供了定性结果（图6），展示了检测结果在RGB图像上的投影。
case_study.findings: 可视化显示VoxelNet能够检测出各种场景下的汽车、行人和自行车。

benchmark.description: 在KITTI 3D目标检测基准上评估，该基准包含汽车、行人、自行车三类，以及Easy、Moderate、Hard三个难度级别。
benchmark.findings: VoxelNet在KITTI验证集和测试集上均取得了当时最先进的性能。

efficiency.description: 报告了推理时间：在TitanX GPU和1.7GHz CPU上，整个网络（包括体素化、VFE、卷积中间层和RPN）耗时约30毫秒。
efficiency.findings: 30毫秒的推理时间表明模型具有一定的实时性潜力。

risk_flags: 仅报告了单个GPU上的推理时间，未提供详细的计算复杂度分析或与其他方法的效率比较。

evidence.description: 论文详细描述了高效实现方法，包括哈希表索引、密集缓冲区构建和GPU并行处理。
论文报告了30毫秒的推理时间，表明模型具有一定的实时性潜力。

terms.definition: 体积像素，是3D空间中的立方体单元，用于离散化连续空间。
terms.context: VoxelNet将点云划分为等间距的体素网格。

terms.definition: VoxelNet的核心层，将每个体素内的点组转换为统一的特征表示，通过结合点特征和局部聚合特征来编码局部3D形状信息。
terms.context: 堆叠多个VFE层以学习复杂特征。

terms.definition: 一种用于生成候选目标区域（提议）的卷积神经网络，在VoxelNet中用于从体积特征图生成3D边界框预测。
terms.context: RPN接收卷积中间层的输出，生成概率分数图和回归图。

terms.definition: 一种数据结构，仅存储非零（或非空）元素及其坐标，用于高效表示高维稀疏数据。
terms.context: VoxelNet将非空体素的特征表示为稀疏4D张量，以减少内存和计算开销。

terms.definition: 从正上方俯视3D场景的2D投影，常用于3D目标检测中简化问题。
terms.context: 论文将VoxelNet与基于鸟瞰图特征的方法（如HC-baseline）进行比较。

terms.definition: 预定义的具有特定尺寸和方向的参考边界框，用于目标检测中的候选框生成和回归。
terms.context: VoxelNet为汽车、行人、自行车定义了不同的锚框尺寸和旋转。

terms.definition: 衡量两个边界框重叠程度的指标，计算为交集面积除以并集面积。
terms.context: 用于锚框与地面真值框的匹配，以及评估检测性能。

required_datasets: KITTI 3D目标检测基准（包含7,481个训练点云和7,518个测试点云）
required_models: VoxelNet网络架构（包括VFE层、卷积中间层、RPN）
required_compute: GPU（如TitanX），用于训练和推理。论文报告推理时间约30ms。
reproduction.code_available: 未知（论文未提及代码是否公开）。

steps.description: 1. 数据准备：下载KITTI数据集，按照论文描述的协议划分训练集和验证集（3,712训练，3,769验证）。
2. 数据预处理：实现体素划分、分组和随机采样（T=35用于汽车，T=45用于行人/自行车）。
3. 模型实现：实现VFE层（VFE-1(7,32), VFE-2(32,128)）、卷积中间层（Conv3D层序列）和RPN（图4架构）。
4. 损失函数：实现总损失函数（公式2），包括二元交叉熵分类损失和SmoothL1回归损失，设置α=1.5, β=1。
5. 训练细节：使用SGD，学习率0.01（前150 epochs），0.001（最后10 epochs），批大小16。实现数据增强（对边界框的扰动、全局旋转）。
6. 锚框设置：为汽车、行人、自行车分别设置锚框尺寸、中心高度和旋转（0°和90°）。
7. 评估：在KITTI验证集上计算鸟瞰图和全3D检测的平均精度（AP）。
8. 高效实现：实现哈希表进行点云索引，构建密集输入缓冲区以支持GPU并行处理。

metadata.title: VoxelNet: End-to-End Learning for Point Cloud Based 3D Object Detection
metadata.venue: 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Object Detection / Computer Vision / Face Recognition / Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Accurate detection of objects in 3D point clouds is a central problem in many applications, such as autonomous navigation, housekeeping robots, and augmented/virtual reality. To interface a highly sparse LiDAR point cloud with a region proposal network (RPN), most existing efforts have focused on hand-crafted feature representations, for example, a bird's eye view projection. In this work, we remove the need of manual feature engineering for 3D point clouds and propose VoxelNet, a generic 3D detection network that unifies feature extraction and bounding box prediction into a single stage, end-to-end trainable deep network. Specifically, VoxelNet divides a point cloud into equally spaced 3D voxels and transforms a group of points within each voxel into a unified feature representation through the newly introduced voxel feature encoding (VFE) layer. In this way, the point cloud is encoded as a descriptive volumetric representation, which is then connected to a RPN to generate detections. Experiments on the KITTI car detection benchmark show that VoxelNet outperforms the state-of-the-art LiDAR based 3D detection methods by a large margin. Furthermore, our network learns an effective discriminative representation of objects with various geometries, leading to encouraging results in 3D detection of pedestrians and cyclists, based on only LiDAR.

Abstract

Accurate detection of objects in 3D point clouds is a central problem in many applications, such as autonomous navigation, housekeeping robots, and augmented/virtual re- ality. To interface a highly sparse LiDAR point cloud with a region proposal network (RPN), most existing efforts have focused on hand-crafted feature representations, for exam- ple, a bird’s eye view projection. In this work, we remove the need of manual feature engineering for 3D point clouds and propose VoxelNet, a generic 3D detection network that uniﬁes feature extraction and bounding box prediction into a single stage, end-to-end trainable deep network. Speciﬁ- cally, VoxelNet divides a point cloud into equally spaced 3D voxels and transforms a group of points within each voxel into a uniﬁed feature representation through the newly in- troduced voxel feature encoding (VFE) layer. In this way, the point cloud is encoded as a descriptive volumetric rep- resentation, which is then connected to a RPN to generate det...
LiDAR based 3D detection methods by a large margin. Fur-
thermore, our network learns an effective discriminative

representation of objects with various geometries, leading to encouraging results in 3D detection of pedestrians and cyclists, based on only LiDAR. 1. Introduction Point cloud based 3D object detection is an important component of a variety of real-world applications, such as autonomous navigation [11, 14], housekeeping robots [26], and augmented/virtual reality [27]. Compared to image- based detection, LiDAR provides reliable depth informa- tion that can be used to accurately localize objects and characterize their shapes [21, 5]. However, unlike im- ages, LiDAR point clouds are sparse and have highly vari- able point density, due to factors such as non-uniform sampling of the 3D space, effective range of the sensors, occlusion, and the relative pose. To handle these chal- lenges, many approaches manually crafted feature represen-
Figure 1. V oxelNet directly operates on the raw point cloud (no

need for feature engineering) and produces the 3D detection re- sults using a single end-to-end trainable network. tations for point clouds that are tuned for 3D object detec- tion. Several methods project point clouds into a perspec- tive view and apply image-based feature extraction tech- niques [28, 15, 22]. Other approaches rasterize point clouds into a 3D voxel grid and encode each voxel with hand- crafted features [41, 9, 37, 38, 21, 5]. However, these man- ual design choices introduce an information bottleneck that prevents these approaches from effectively exploiting 3D shape information and the required invariances for the de- tection task. A major breakthrough in recognition [20] and detection [13] tasks on images was due to moving from hand-crafted features to machine-learned features. Recently, Qi et al. [29] proposed PointNet, an end-to- end deep neural network that learns point-wise features di- rectly from point clouds. This approach demonstrated im- pressive results on...
Figure 2. V oxelNet architecture. The feature learning network takes a raw point cloud as input, partitions the space into voxels, and

transforms points within each voxel to a vector representation characterizing the shape information. The space is represented as a sparse 4D tensor. The convolutional middle layers processes the 4D tensor to aggregate spatial context. Finally, a RPN generates the 3D detection. tures as in [29, 30] results in high computational and mem- ory requirements. Scaling up 3D feature learning networks to orders of magnitude more points and to 3D detection tasks are the main challenges that we address in this paper. Region proposal network (RPN) [32] is a highly opti- mized algorithm for efﬁcient object detection [17, 5, 31, 24]. However, this approach requires data to be dense and organized in a tensor structure (e.g. image, video) which is not the case for typical LiDAR point clouds. In this pa- per, we close the gap between point set feature learning and RPN for 3D detection task. We present V oxelNet, a generic 3D detection framework
that simultaneously learns a discriminative feature represen-

tation from point clouds and predicts accurate 3D bounding boxes, in an end-to-end fashion, as shown in Figure 2. We design a novel voxel feature encoding (VFE) layer, which enables inter-point interaction within a voxel, by combin- ing point-wise features with a locally aggregated feature. Stacking multiple VFE layers allows learning complex fea- tures for characterizing local 3D shape information. Specif- ically, V oxelNet divides the point cloud into equally spaced 3D voxels, encodes each voxel via stacked VFE layers, and then 3D convolution further aggregates local voxel features,
transforming the point cloud into a high-dimensional volu-

metric representation. Finally, a RPN consumes the vol- umetric representation and yields the detection result. This efﬁcient algorithm beneﬁts both from the sparse point struc- ture and efﬁcient parallel processing on the voxel grid. We evaluate V oxelNet on the bird’s eye view detection and the full 3D detection tasks, provided by the KITTI benchmark [11]. Experimental results show that V oxelNet outperforms the state-of-the-art LiDAR based 3D detection
methods by a large margin. We also demonstrate that V oxel-
Net achieves highly encouraging results in detecting pedes- trians and cyclists from LiDAR point cloud. 1.1. Related Work
Rapid development of 3D sensor technology has moti-

vated researchers to develop efﬁcient representations to de- tect and localize objects in point clouds. Some of the earlier methods for feature representation are [39, 8, 7, 19, 40, 33, 6, 25, 1, 34, 2]. These hand-crafted features yield satisfac- tory results when rich and detailed 3D shape information is available. However their inability to adapt to more complex shapes and scenes, and learn required invariances from data resulted in limited success for uncontrolled scenarios such as autonomous navigation. Given that images provide detailed texture information, many algorithms infered the 3D bounding boxes from 2D images [4, 3, 42, 43, 44, 36]. However, the accuracy of image-based 3D detection approaches are bounded by the accuracy of the depth estimation. Several LIDAR based 3D object detection techniques utilize a voxel grid representation. [41, 9] encode each nonempty voxel with 6 statistical quantities that are de- rived from all the points contained within the voxel. [37] fuses...

schemes [28, 15, 22]. There are also several multi-modal fusion methods that combine images and LiDAR to improve detection accu- racy [10, 16, 5]. These methods provide improved perfor- mance compared to LiDAR-only 3D detection, particularly for small objects (pedestrians, cyclists) or when the objects are far, since cameras provide an order of magnitude more measurements than LiDAR. However the need for an addi- tional camera that is time synchronized and calibrated with the LiDAR restricts their use and makes the solution more sensitive to sensor failure modes. In this work we focus on LiDAR-only detection. 1.2. Contributions • We propose a novel end-to-end trainable deep archi- tecture for point-cloud-based 3D detection, V oxelNet, that directly operates on sparse 3D points and avoids information bottlenecks introduced by manual feature engineering. • We present an efﬁcient method to implement V oxelNet which beneﬁts both from the sparse point structure and efﬁcient parallel proces...
2.1.1 Feature Learning Network

Voxel Partition Given a point cloud, we subdivide the 3D space into equally spaced voxels as shown in Figure 2. Sup- pose the point cloud encompasses 3D space with range D, H,W along the Z, Y , X axes respectively. We deﬁne each voxel of size vD, vH, and vW accordingly. The resulting
3D voxel grid is of size D′ = D/vD,H′ = H/vH,W′ =

W/vW . Here, for simplicity, we assume D, H, W are a multiple ofvD,vH,vW . Grouping We group the points according to the voxel they reside in. Due to factors such as distance, occlusion, ob- ject’s relative pose, and non-uniform sampling, the LiDAR Fully Connected Neural Net Point-wise Input Point-wise Feature Element-wise Maxpool Point-wise Concatenate Locally Aggregated Feature Point-wise concatenated Feature

An illustration is shown in Figure 2, where V oxel-1 has signiﬁcantly more points than V oxel-2 and V oxel-4, while V oxel-3 contains no point. Random Sampling Typically a high-deﬁnition LiDAR point cloud is composed of ∼100k points. Directly pro- cessing all the points not only imposes increased mem- ory/efﬁciency burdens on the computing platform, but also highly variable point density throughout the space might bias the detection. To this end, we randomly sample a ﬁxed number, T , of points from those voxels containing more than T points. This sampling strategy has two purposes, (1) computational savings (see Section 2.3 for details); and (2) decreases the imbalance of points between the voxels which reduces the sampling bias, and adds more variation to training. Sparse Tensor Representation By processing only the non-empty voxels, we obtain a list of voxel features, each uniquely associated to the spatial coordinates of a particu- lar non-empty voxel. The obtained list of voxel-wise fea- tures can be represented as a sparse 4D tensor, of size C×D′×H′×W′ as shown in Figure 2. Although the point cloud contains∼100k points, more than 90% of vox- els typically are empty. Representing non-empty voxel fea- tures as a sparse tensor greatly reduces the memory usage and computation cost during backpropagation, and it is a critical step in our efﬁcient implementation.

We use Conv MD(cin,c out, k, s, p) to represent an M- dimensional convolution operator where cin and cout are the number of input and output channels,k, s, and p are the M-dimensional vectors corresponding to kernel size, stride size and padding size respectively. When the size across the M-dimensions are the same, we use a scalar to represent
the size e.g.k for k = (k,k,k ).

Each convolutional middle layer applies 3D convolution, BN layer, and ReLU layer sequentially. The convolutional middle layers aggregate voxel-wise features within a pro- gressively expanding receptive ﬁeld, adding more context to the shape description. The detailed sizes of the ﬁlters in the convolutional middle layers are explained in Section 3.
2.1.3 Region Proposal Network
Recently, region proposal networks [32] have become an
important building block of top-performing object detec-

tion frameworks [38, 5, 23]. In this work, we make several key modiﬁcations to the RPN architecture proposed in [32], and combine it with the feature learning network and con- volutional middle layers to form an end-to-end trainable pipeline. The input to our RPN is the feature map provided by the convolutional middle layers. The architecture of this network is illustrated in Figure 4. The network has three blocks of fully convolutional layers. The ﬁrst layer of each block downsamples the feature map by half via a convolu- tion with a stride size of 2, followed by a sequence of con- volutions of stride 1 (×q meansq applications of the ﬁlter). After each convolution layer, BN and ReLU operations are applied. We then upsample the output of every block to a ﬁxed size and concatanate to construct the high resolution feature map. Efﬁcient Implementation GPUs are optimized for processing dense tensor struc- tures. The problem with working directly with the point cloud is that the points are sparsely distributed across space and each voxel has a variable number of points. We devised a method that converts the point cloud into a dense tensor structure where stacked VFE operations can be processed in parallel across points and voxels. The method is summarized in Figure 5. We initialize a K×T× 7 dimensional tensor structure to store the voxel
input feature buffer where K is the maximum number of
non-empty voxels, T is the maximum number of points

per voxel, and 7 is the input encoding dimension for each point. The points are randomized before processing. For each point in the point cloud, we check if the corresponding voxel already exists. This lookup operation is done efﬁ- ciently in O(1) using a hash table where the voxel coordi- nate is used as the hash key. If the voxel is already initial- ized we insert the point to the voxel location if there are less thanT points, otherwise the point is ignored. If the voxel is not initialized, we initialize a new voxel, store its coordi- nate in the voxel coordinate buffer, and insert the point to this voxel location. The voxel input feature and coordinate buffers can be constructed via a single pass over the point list, therefore its complexity is O(n). To further improve the memory/compute efﬁciency it is possible to only store

The ﬁrst form of data augmentation applies perturbation independently to each ground truth 3D bounding box to- gether with those LiDAR points within the box. Speciﬁ- cally, around Z-axis we rotatebi and the associated Ωi with respect to (xc,y c,z c) by a uniformally distributed random variable ∆θ∈ [−π/10, +π/10]. Then we add a translation (∆x, ∆y, ∆z) to the XYZ components of bi and to each point in Ωi, where ∆x, ∆y, ∆z are drawn independently from a Gaussian distribution with mean zero and standard deviation 1.0. To avoid physically impossible outcomes, we perform a collision test between any two boxes after the per- turbation and revert to the original if a collision is detected. Since the perturbation is applied to each ground truth box and the associated LiDAR points independently, the net- work is able to learn from substantially more variations than from the original training data. Conclusion Most existing methods in LiDAR-based 3D detection rely on hand-crafted feature representations, for example, a bird’s eye view projection. In this paper, we remove the bottleneck of manual feature engineering and propose V ox- elNet, a novel end-to-end trainable deep architecture for point cloud based 3D detection. Our approach can operate directly on sparse 3D points and capture 3D shape infor- mation effectively. We also present an efﬁcient implemen- tation of V oxelNet that beneﬁts from point cloud sparsity and parallel processing on a voxel grid. Our experiments on the KITTI car detection task show that V oxelNet outper- forms state-of-the-art LiDAR based 3D detection methods
by a large margin. On more challenging tasks, such as 3D

detection of pedestrians and cyclists, V oxelNet also demon- strates encouraging results showing that it provides a better 3D representation. Future work includes extending V oxel- Net for joint LiDAR and image based end-to-end 3D detec- tion to further improve detection and localization accuracy.
